experiment: M4 Splay GC live/peak occupancy diagnostic

source.instrumentation: profile-memory-only QUENCH_MEMORY snapshot after every collection: pre-GC occupied slots and allocation count, post-GC survivor counts and tracked payload bytes by CellKind. The source change is measurement-only and is reverted after capture.

host.resource_limits: 10 logical CPUs and 16 GiB physical memory; no cgroup CPU or memory quota on macOS.

build.command: CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/iteration/task61-splay-gc-profile-20261009 cargo build --profile production -p quench-node --features profile-memory

summary.interpretation: The large-set collections do reach about 2x survivors immediately before GC, as the policy predicts. But the Splay run ends with 1.466M live cells against 1.562M heap slots: peak/final live is only 1.066x, so the roughly 2x collection-boundary ratio does not translate into a 2x peak-to-final-live RSS model. The tracked payload-byte ratio is also about 1.062x. The large majority of slot capacity is required by the live set at this fixture endpoint; do not infer a 120 MB reducible headroom from this run.

prior_linux_result: The previous 11-pair Linux live/2 experiment reduced Splay median RSS by 54.4 MB but regressed Score 16.94% (95% interval entirely negative); see task61-splay-gc-threshold-2026-10-08.json.
decision: Do not run the 1.0/0.5/0.25/0.125 M4 threshold campaign from this evidence alone. The current M4 profile puts peak live only 6.6% above end-of-run live, and the prior 0.5 Linux experiment had a clear Score regression. Revisit only with a new memory breakdown showing a sizeable GC-controlled component.
